layers.name: Resources
layers.description: What supports the chain. Energy, water, fabs, materials, skilled trades, the inputs the entire stack consumes.
layers.detail: Before chips, before data centers, before models, there's power, water, foundries, rare earths, and the humans who build it all. When AI demand explodes, the bottleneck isn't algorithms. It's megawatts and skilled trades.
layers.verdict: The real bottleneck. Slow to build, impossible to fake.

sublayers.name: Energy & Grid Interconnect
sublayers.description: Power generation, PPAs, transmission, and the multi-year grid-interconnect queue, the megawatts the stack consumes and the wait to get them switched on

sublayers.name: Thermal & Water Management
sublayers.description: Cooling systems, water access, immersion/liquid cooling, heat reuse, the thermodynamic ceiling on every GPU cluster

sublayers.name: Fabrication & Foundry
sublayers.description: Leading-edge chip fabrication capacity, EUV lithography, advanced packaging (CoWoS), the physical floor of L0

sublayers.name: Critical Materials & Supply Chain
sublayers.description: Rare earths, lithium, cobalt, gallium, specialty substrates, and the refining, logistics, and geopolitical chokepoints that gate them

sublayers.name: Skilled Trades & Human Capital
sublayers.description: Electricians, HVAC techs, data-center builders, fab process engineers, robotics technicians, the labor pool no model can synthesize

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.description: The shovels. Chips, data centers, networking, cloud, edge, what is needed to process intelligence.
layers.detail: The compute substrate. NVIDIA doesn't care which model wins, they sell to all of them. When L2 commoditizes, value accrues to L0.
layers.verdict: Shovel sellers win every gold rush.

sublayers.name: Silicon & Memory
sublayers.description: GPUs, TPUs, custom AI accelerators, plus HBM and high-bandwidth memory (SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung), the invisible bottleneck behind every chip cycle

sublayers.name: Data Centers
sublayers.description: Physical facilities housing compute at scale

sublayers.name: Interconnect Fabric
sublayers.description: Networking between chips, racks, regions, clouds

sublayers.name: Compute & State Infrastructure
sublayers.description: On-demand compute, scheduling, and durable agent state (checkpointing, workflow state, runtime memory stores)

sublayers.name: Edge & On-Device Compute
sublayers.description: Local inference on phones, vehicles, sensors, endpoints

layers.name: Data
layers.description: The raw input. What data do you have that nobody else can get?
layers.detail: Proprietary datasets are the raw fuel. More agents = more demand for data. The L1b test: if your data is public, the model layer wins.

sublayers.name: Public & Open Data
sublayers.description: Common Crawl, Wikipedia, government data, open datasets

sublayers.name: Proprietary Data
sublayers.description: Licensed, paywalled, or internally generated training corpora

sublayers.name: Behavioral & Sensor Data
sublayers.description: Clicks, sessions, interaction logs, and camera, LiDAR, IMU, telemetry, and physical-world sensor streams for robotics and autonomy

sublayers.name: Outcome Data
sublayers.description: Labels, results, conversions, win/loss, audit trails, what actually happened after the model acted

sublayers.name: Synthetic & Simulation Data
sublayers.description: Machine-generated corpora and simulated environments (Isaac Sim, CARLA, Omniverse, world-sim) for training, augmentation, and embodied agent rollout

layers.name: Models
layers.description: Intelligence refinement. Rent early, build custom at scale.
layers.detail: Foundation models are the smelters, expensive, few can operate at scale. Once refined, the gold is a commodity, which is why model providers need to move up the chain.

sublayers.name: Foundation & Multimodal Models
sublayers.description: Large pre-trained generalists, GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, and vision-language-action and video models (Sora, Veo) that span text, image, audio, and motion

sublayers.name: Specialized & Fine-Tuned Models
sublayers.description: Domain-tuned, distilled, and PEFT/LoRA-adapted models for specific verticals or tasks (BloombergGPT, Med-PaLM, Codestral)

sublayers.name: Embedding & Retrieval
sublayers.description: Vector representations, search indices, reranking, and RAG infrastructure

sublayers.name: Model Routing & Composition
sublayers.description: Selecting, chaining, ensembling, or mixture-of-experts routing across multiple models per task to balance cost, latency, and quality

sublayers.name: Reasoning & World Models
sublayers.description: Extended chain-of-thought, planning, and multi-step inference, plus predictive world models (V-JEPA, Genie, Sora-as-simulator) that let agents and robots imagine outcomes before acting

layers.name: Gatekeeping
layers.description: Trust, acceptance, approval. Can the system be allowed in?
layers.detail: Without the hallmark, no enterprise buyer touches it. L3 is the slowest moat to build and the hardest to replicate.
layers.verdict: Essential. More agents = more access control.

sublayers.name: Compliance & Export Controls
sublayers.description: Regulatory, legal, and policy filters (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, EU AI Act), plus chip export controls, model sovereignty, and data-residency regimes that decide where the stack is allowed to run

sublayers.name: Quality Gates
sublayers.description: Accuracy, hallucination detection, output grading, eval harnesses, regression suites

sublayers.name: Safety, Security & Provenance
sublayers.description: Harmful-content filtering, adversarial defense, prompt-injection protection, and content provenance (C2PA, watermarking, deepfake attestation) that proves what was generated and by whom

sublayers.name: Editorial Gates
sublayers.description: Tone, brand voice, style, taste, the human judgment layer

sublayers.name: Distribution Gates
sublayers.description: App store approval, ranking, marketplace curation, discovery control

layers.name: Access
layers.description: Connectivity, permissions, integrations, the pipes layer.
layers.detail: Grammarly survived because it had railroad tracks (plugins) into Word, Gmail, Chrome. Jasper had no tracks. Deep integrations and agent identity create switching costs.

sublayers.name: API & Integration Layer
sublayers.description: REST/GraphQL endpoints, SDKs, webhooks connecting AI to systems

sublayers.name: Agent Interface Protocols
sublayers.description: MCP, tool-use specs, agent-to-agent communication standards

sublayers.name: Access Governance & Agent Commerce
sublayers.description: Who can use what, RBAC, scoping, audit trails, and agent-payment rails (Stripe/Visa/Mastercard agent-pay, spend limits, programmatic checkout, machine-to-machine billing)

sublayers.name: Real-Time Interaction Infrastructure
sublayers.description: Streaming, voice pipelines, video, low-latency modality transport

sublayers.name: Agent Identity & Provenance
sublayers.description: Verifying which agent acted, credential chains, trust signatures

layers.name: Execution
layers.description: Applied skills and capabilities. Doing the actual work.
layers.detail: A jeweler takes refined gold and crafts rings, necklaces, watches, each requiring specialized skill. L5 is THE entry point for AI-native companies.
layers.verdict: Durable if deep. Generic skills get absorbed.

sublayers.name: Domain Execution & Tool Use
sublayers.description: Doing the actual work, legal drafting, code generation, diagnosis, underwriting, including function calling, code interpreter, browser/computer use, and structured tool invocation that turns a model into an operator

sublayers.name: Decision Frameworks & Reasoning Scaffolds
sublayers.description: Structured thinking patterns, checklists, rubrics the agent follows

sublayers.name: Retrieval-Augmented Workflows
sublayers.description: Grounding execution in retrieved context, knowledge, and documents

sublayers.name: Operating Playbooks
sublayers.description: Company-specific SOPs, rules, preferences encoded for agents

sublayers.name: Interaction Skills & Actuation
sublayers.description: Tone, empathy, negotiation, persuasion, and physical-world actuation (robotic control, valve/vehicle/device operation)

layers.name: Orchestration
layers.description: Workflow, routing, coordination. How skills compose into outcomes.
layers.detail: A single ring is useful. A curated jewelry collection with tasting, fitting, and custom design is an experience. Orchestration composes skills into workflows.
layers.verdict: Contested. Becoming a feature, not a product.

sublayers.name: Agent Loops
sublayers.description: Single-agent plan-act-observe cycles

sublayers.name: Human-in-the-Loop
sublayers.description: Escalation patterns, approval workflows, human override design

sublayers.name: Role Routing & Task Decomposition
sublayers.description: Breaking complex work into subtasks and assigning to the right agent

sublayers.name: Context & State Management
sublayers.description: Maintaining working memory, session state, context windows across steps

sublayers.name: Runtime Assurance & Learning Loops
sublayers.description: Post-deployment monitoring, evals, feedback pipelines, drift detection

layers.name: Surface
layers.description: Interface, presentation, experience. How the user meets the intelligence.
layers.detail: People see the ring on the finger, the surface, the sparkle. If all you own is the display case (L7), anyone can build another display case. Embedded and transactional surfaces are the moats.

sublayers.name: Conversational
sublayers.description: Voice and chat interfaces, the talking layer

sublayers.name: Visual Interfaces & Media
sublayers.description: Dashboards, generated images, video, rich media output

sublayers.name: Embedded & Embodied AI
sublayers.description: AI woven into existing tools (IDE copilots, email assistants, in-app agents) and embodied in physical hardware (robots, devices, vehicles)

sublayers.name: Transaction Surface
sublayers.description: Where the AI closes a deal, books an appointment, processes a payment

sublayers.name: Async & Ambient Surfaces
sublayers.description: Background agents, notifications, proactive nudges, always-on monitoring

layers.name: Memory
layers.description: Retention, learning, compounding context. What the system remembers.
layers.detail: The jeweler keeps records: which designs sold, which metals each customer prefers. Over time, this memory makes every decision better. Memory is the only layer that gets stronger every day.
layers.verdict: The ultimate moat. Memory that compounds wins.

sublayers.name: Session & Short-Term Memory
sublayers.description: Within-conversation context, scratch state, working memory

sublayers.name: User & Entity Profiles
sublayers.description: Persistent preferences, history, relationship context per user or account

sublayers.name: Aggregated Network Learning
sublayers.description: Patterns learned across many users/customers, fleet intelligence

sublayers.name: Institutional Knowledge
sublayers.description: What the organization knows, docs, decisions, tribal knowledge encoded

sublayers.name: Learned World Models
sublayers.description: The system's accumulated causal understanding of how things work
